reviews.title: Real nice case for ATX motherboard!!
reviews.comment: No vertical mount for the graphics card, but that is fine, would not have used it anyway!! This is a nice case and everything is running cool!! Got some 120mm wire guards for the bottom fans. The LCD Corsair 360mm liquid cooler fit very well. MSI Z890 Carbon WIFI motherboard and Core Ultra 7 265k CPU are running in the mid 30's without much of a load. Ten fans all total and the tempered glass side panel looks great!!

reviews.title: Fantastic case with small imperfections
reviews.comment:
It's a great case with a few small points that could be better, but aren't bad.
It's well constructed and feels solid.  Definitelyan EATX case, which is hard to always pin down when liking fit cases, but you'll still want to make sure you route your CPU power cables BEFORE you mount the motherboard and AIO if you're using one because they'll both make plugging cpu power in next to impossible if you don't.
The preinstalled fans looks nice and run quietly; they're good quality ARGB fans, though you should know that the bottom fans are not RGB and are one single triple fan plate.
If your looking for rgb fans in the bottom to blow up into the gpu, you'll need to remove the 3 fan plate and install 3 of your own for that.
Airflow is perfect with a top mounted AIO radiator.  If you aren't using an AIO, you'll want to install your own top fans for more exhaust or intake as you see fit.
There's plenty of space in the bottom as well as the rear side panel for excellent cable management, hiding any fan/rgb hubs you might want and so on.
All in all, this case feels nicely premium to build in and strikes a great balance between efficient use of space and comfortable working area for your build.
For a full tower case, it's not wildly huge and isn't going to take up a bigger footprint than most midtown cases do.
Main Complaints -
The tempered glass panel is affixed by a hand screw rather than just snapped in as on more premium brands, but it does mean it has more stability in thy end.  It does snap as well and I suspect you could leave the hand screw out but I'm not sure if it's solidly clipped in enough for that by the clips alone.
The tempered glass side panel is also difficult to remove without also removing the top panel, which is affixed by two hand screws.  You can do it but it's very snug and won't seem at first lile you even can.

reviews.title: Seller confirmed, no Vertical GPU mount, unlike description states. Not good Quality to price
reviews.comment:
-1 Star for misinformation and -1 Star for price to quality. However, the design is goodin general.
Negatives : If you plan to vertically mount your GPU, This case (Black) has NO vertical Mount included in the box, even though it clearly states otherwise.  Ask, seller about the White one before buying.  For the price of the case it is disappointing that it is not included (to and confirmed with seller, especially how its build feels cheap. For example bottom dust mesh is plastic, so before handling the case during your hardware install, remove it. The front panel grid also feels plastic with a non-removable metal dust mesh attached to the panel.  The back area around PSU is also a grid without a dust mesh that will allow some dusty airflow, but other places are well protected from dust. I scotch taped my back-side grid around the PSU, which is not visible.  Last negative, if you plan on using both 3.5" and 2.5" drive bays, one power SATA cable potentially won't be enough to reach for both locations.
Positives: Airflow is definitely good. It dropped my GPU temps by 10C during furmark compared to my old case that also had case fans.
The snap-on type cover panels (top, front and sides) are a great design.  It will definitely be easy to clean, though I don't know how many removal/snapping back in place cycles can the front panel handle.  Also, cable management is quite well thought out., outside of the distance between 3.5" and 2.5" bays.
This one is debatable:  the bottom "three" fans are actually a panel with 3 fans and no RGB. It has only 1 power cable feeding all three fans, which was a benefit to me. I don't care about it missing RGB as I don't see it anyway when sitting. The other 4 fans are proper 120mm fans with RGB.
Note, the front panel should be able to support 3 140mm fans based on tape measurement though I didn't try. It might be tight placing all three in, so a word of caution. Also, my MB has aRGB and case fan sockets at the bottom, I had to rearrange the plug connections between the front panel fans to allow them to reach those locations. The back side fan did not have long enough cable to reach the bottom sockets on the MB, so I sent this one to the top.
Afterthought, with the quality, I would doubt that if the vertical mount for GPU was included it would be any good.
